q: How do I deselect an edit point?
a: Toggle Trim Type (`trim.toggleType`) switches the selected edit between a regular trim, a ripple trim and a rolling edit; `trim.clear` deselects. Select Nearest Edit Point (`trim.selectNearest`) picks the cut closest to the playhead on the targeted tracks, and several can be selected to trim tracks together.

q: What trim types can an edit point have?
a: Toggle Trim Type (`trim.toggleType`) switches the selected edit between a regular trim, a ripple trim and a rolling edit; `trim.clear` deselects. Select Nearest Edit Point (`trim.selectNearest`) picks the cut closest to the playhead on the targeted tracks, and several can be selected to trim tracks together.

q: What do the trim-to-playhead commands do?
a: Ripple Trim Previous / Next Edit to Playhead (`trim.ripplePrevious`, `trim.rippleNext`) cut from the playhead back to the previous edit (or on to the next) and close the gap; Trim Previous / Next Edit to Playhead (`trim.previous`, `trim.next`) do the same leaving a gap. Extend Selected Edit to Playhead moves the selected edit there; Extend Previous / Next Edit moves the nearest one. Ripple keeps everything after in sync; plain ones are safer when other tracks must not move.

q: What's the difference between Trim and Ripple Trim to Playhead?
a: Ripple Trim Previous / Next Edit to Playhead (`trim.ripplePrevious`, `trim.rippleNext`) cut from the playhead back to the previous edit (or on to the next) and close the gap; Trim Previous / Next Edit to Playhead (`trim.previous`, `trim.next`) do the same leaving a gap. Extend Selected Edit to Playhead moves the selected edit there; Extend Previous / Next Edit moves the nearest one. Ripple keeps everything after in sync; plain ones are safer when other tracks must not move.

q: In Resolve I'd use Trim End to Playhead. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Use Trim Next Edit to Playhead (`trim.next`, leaves a gap) or Ripple Trim Next Edit to Playhead (`trim.rippleNext`, closes it); the Previous versions trim the start.

q: How does dynamic trimming work?
a: With an edit point selected, J, K and L shuttle the edit instead of the playhead (`trim.shuttle`): the cut follows playback and stops where you stop (`trim.shuttleStop`); `trim.cancelDynamic` throws the change away. Play Around Edit plays a few seconds either side. `trim.monitor` reports the Trim monitor's outgoing and incoming frames for agents.

q: What does the Trim monitor show?
a: With an edit point selected, J, K and L shuttle the edit instead of the playhead (`trim.shuttle`): the cut follows playback and stops where you stop (`trim.shuttleStop`); `trim.cancelDynamic` throws the change away. Play Around Edit plays a few seconds either side. `trim.monitor` reports the Trim monitor's outgoing and incoming frames for agents.

q: What is the Source monitor for?
a: The Source monitor shows a clip before it goes on the timeline: double-click it in the Project panel (`source.open`), mark In and Out, then Insert (`source.insert`) or Overwrite (`source.overwrite`) at the timeline's playhead on the source-patched tracks. `source.setPlayhead` and `source.inspect` drive it from scripts.

q: How do I drive the Source monitor from a script?
a: The Source monitor shows a clip before it goes on the timeline: double-click it in the Project panel (`source.open`), mark In and Out, then Insert (`source.insert`) or Overwrite (`source.overwrite`) at the timeline's playhead on the source-patched tracks. `source.setPlayhead` and `source.inspect` drive it from scripts.

q: How do I record multicam cuts from a script?
a: `multicam.recordStart` / `recordStop` turn recording on and off; with it on each angle click becomes a cut, without it `multicam.cut` / `multicam.switchAngle` change the angle at the playhead. `multicam.autoAdjustQuality` lowers the preview quality so many angles play smoothly; `multicam.gridLayout` and the page commands handle many cameras.

q: What does multicam.autoAdjustQuality do?
a: `multicam.recordStart` / `recordStop` turn recording on and off; with it on each angle click becomes a cut, without it `multicam.cut` / `multicam.switchAngle` change the angle at the playhead. `multicam.autoAdjustQuality` lowers the preview quality so many angles play smoothly; `multicam.gridLayout` and the page commands handle many cameras.

q: Is a slider drag one undo step?
a: Every command is one undo step, and a slider drag is one step, not one per frame: Undo (`edit.undo`, Cmd+Z) and Redo (`edit.redo`). The history keeps the last 200 steps and is cleared when you open or make another project.

q: Does undo history survive opening another project?
a: Every command is one undo step, and a slider drag is one step, not one per frame: Undo (`edit.undo`, Cmd+Z) and Redo (`edit.redo`). The history keeps the last 200 steps and is cleared when you open or make another project.

q: Which attributes can Paste Attributes copy?
a: Paste Attributes… (`edit.pasteAttributes`) gives the selected clips the copied clip's chosen attributes: Motion, Opacity, Time Remapping, Volume, Panner, effects. Remove Attributes… takes chosen ones off. Paste drops clips at the playhead over what's there; Paste Insert pushes later clips along. Duplicate (`edit.duplicate`) copies a project item.

q: What does Duplicate do in the Project panel?
a: Paste Attributes… (`edit.pasteAttributes`) gives the selected clips the copied clip's chosen attributes: Motion, Opacity, Time Remapping, Volume, Panner, effects. Remove Attributes… takes chosen ones off. Paste drops clips at the playhead over what's there; Paste Insert pushes later clips along. Duplicate (`edit.duplicate`) copies a project item.

q: How do I search the project for a clip name?
a: Find… / Find Next (`edit.find`, `edit.findNext`) search names. Label (`edit.label`, one command per colour such as `edit.label.green`) colours clips and items, and Select Label Group (`edit.selectLabelGroup`) selects everything with the same label. Select All Matching selects every timeline clip from the same media.

q: How do I select every clip with the same label?
a: Find… / Find Next (`edit.find`, `edit.findNext`) search names. Label (`edit.label`, one command per colour such as `edit.label.green`) colours clips and items, and Select Label Group (`edit.selectLabelGroup`) selects everything with the same label. Select All Matching selects every timeline clip from the same media.

q: In Resolve I'd set clip colours. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Use Edit ▸ Label (`edit.label` with a colour, e.g. `edit.label.green`) on the selected clips or items; Select Label Group then selects all clips of that colour.

q: In Resolve I'd use Remove Unused Clips. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Edit ▸ Remove Unused (`edit.removeUnused`) takes items no sequence uses out of the project; the files stay on disk. Consolidate Duplicates merges items that point at the same file.

q: What can I change in Sequence Settings?
a: Sequence Settings… (`sequence.settings`) sets frame size, frame rate, pixel aspect and audio sample rate; Sequence Presets are ready-made sets. Add Tracks… / Delete Tracks… add or remove several at once; `sequence.deleteTrack` removes one. Colour settings have their own dialog (Sequence ▸ Color Management).

q: How do I delete a track?
a: Sequence Settings… (`sequence.settings`) sets frame size, frame rate, pixel aspect and audio sample rate; Sequence Presets are ready-made sets. Add Tracks… / Delete Tracks… add or remove several at once; `sequence.deleteTrack` removes one. Colour settings have their own dialog (Sequence ▸ Color Management).

q: In Resolve I'd open Timeline Settings. Where is that here?
a: Sequence ▸ Sequence Settings… (Timeline in the Resolve workflow) for frame size, frame rate, pixel aspect and audio sample rate.

q: How do I find gaps in my sequence?
a: Jump to the next or previous gap (`sequence.goToNextGap`, `goToPrevGap`, `…InTrack` for one track) and close a selected one with Close Gap (`sequence.closeGap`). Selection Follows Playhead (`sequence.selectionFollowsPlayhead`) selects the clip under the playhead as it moves. Make Subsequence (`sequence.makeSubsequence`, Shift+U) makes a new sequence from the selected clips.

q: What is Selection Follows Playhead?
a: Jump to the next or previous gap (`sequence.goToNextGap`, `goToPrevGap`, `…InTrack` for one track) and close a selected one with Close Gap (`sequence.closeGap`). Selection Follows Playhead (`sequence.selectionFollowsPlayhead`) selects the clip under the playhead as it moves. Make Subsequence (`sequence.makeSubsequence`, Shift+U) makes a new sequence from the selected clips.

q: What does Make Subsequence do?

q: How do I open a nested sequence at the current frame?
a: `sequence.revealNested` opens a nested sequence at the frame. Match Frame (`sequence.matchFrame`) opens a clip's source at the same frame in the Source monitor, and Reverse Match Frame finds the Source monitor's frame on the timeline.

q: How do I delete render files?
a: Render Selection, Render In to Out and Render Audio (`sequence.renderAudio`) do now what the background render cache would do later. Delete Render Files (`sequence.deleteRenderFiles`; `…InToOut` for the marked range) removes them.

q: Can I render just the audio?
a: Render Selection, Render In to Out and Render Audio (`sequence.renderAudio`) do now what the background render cache would do later. Delete Render Files (`sequence.deleteRenderFiles`; `…InToOut` for the marked range) removes them.

q: How do I make a new empty sequence?
a: New ▸ Sequence… (`file.newSequence`) makes an empty sequence; Sequence From Clip matches a clip's size and frame rate. Save All (`file.saveAll`) saves every open project; Close Project and its variants close them.

q: How do I save every open project at once?
a: New ▸ Sequence… (`file.newSequence`) makes an empty sequence; Sequence From Clip matches a clip's size and frame rate. Save All (`file.saveAll`) saves every open project; Close Project and its variants close them.

q: In Resolve I'd set Working Folders. Where's that here?
a: File ▸ Project Settings ▸ Scratch Disks… (`file.projectSettings.scratchDisks`) sets where captured audio and video, preview files and auto-saves go; General… holds the project's general settings.

q: How do I put selected items into a new bin?
a: Bin From Selection (`file.newBinFromSelection`) puts the selected items in a new bin. A Search Bin shows every item matching its rules (a column, a condition and text; several rows, all or any) and updates as the project changes; edit or delete it with `project.editSearchBin` / `project.deleteSearchBin`.

q: How does a search bin decide what to show?
a: Bin From Selection (`file.newBinFromSelection`) puts the selected items in a new bin. A Search Bin shows every item matching its rules (a column, a condition and text; several rows, all or any) and updates as the project changes; edit or delete it with `project.editSearchBin` / `project.deleteSearchBin`.

q: Which formats can Export Frame write?
a: Export Frame (`file.exportFrame`) writes the Program or Source monitor's frame as PNG, JPEG, TIFF or BMP, 8- or 16-bit, optionally imported back. AAF / OMF go to dedicated audio apps; Avid Log Exchange (`file.exportAle`) and Final Cut Pro XML (`file.exportFcp7Xml`) go to other editors. Selection as Revolution Project… writes the selected items as a new project.

q: How do I send part of a project as its own project file?

q: When did Revolution last auto-save?
a: `file.autoSaveStatus` tells when the last auto-save ran; Browse Auto-Saves (`file.listAutoSaves`) lists saved copies to open; `file.recoveryList` lists sessions whose unsaved changes can still be recovered.

q: How do I choose a clip's thumbnail frame?
a: Set Poster Frame (`clip.setPosterFrame`, Cmd+P) picks the frame a clip's thumbnail shows; Clear Poster Frame resets it. Frame Hold Options… chooses which frame a hold shows; Insert Frame Hold Segment cuts in a frozen frame at the playhead.

q: Which frame does a frame hold show?
a: Set Poster Frame (`clip.setPosterFrame`, Cmd+P) picks the frame a clip's thumbnail shows; Clear Poster Frame resets it. Frame Hold Options… chooses which frame a hold shows; Insert Frame Hold Segment cuts in a frozen frame at the playhead.

q: How do I give a clip a new start timecode?
a: Modify ▸ Timecode… (`clip.modifyTimecode`) gives an item a start timecode or tape name, or resets it to the file's own. `clip.audioPeak` reports a clip's peak level. Update Metadata… edits an item's metadata.

q: How do I check a clip's peak level?
